spec: Part VIII 8.1 — weight conversion and record comparison (V52–V53); Appendix A A9 (owner-directed 2026-09-09). Closes the defect where `units` was a display suffix with no conversion: a preference change relabelled every logged weight, changed plate math's physical prescription, and fired a false personal record in one direction while going blind in the other.

vectors.title: a weight converts between units and snaps to the loadable increment
vectors.spec: 8.1 V52; A9 (a logged weight is stored in the unit it was entered in; conversion happens for display only)
vectors.rule: weightIn(value, from, to) returns the value unchanged when from == to; otherwise it converts by the exact international pound (0.45359237 kg) and rounds half-up to the target unit's loadable increment — halves for lb, quarters for kg. Both engines print the same digit.
vectors.reviewNote: The snap is lossy on purpose: a converted weight must name something a gym can actually load. A round trip therefore returns within one display increment, never exactly.

vectors.title: a personal record compares on one normalised scale
vectors.spec: 8.1 V53; A9 (plate math, PR detection and strength trends compare on a normalised value, never on the raw number)
vectors.rule: normalizedForCompare(value, unit) puts a weight on the kilogram scale WITHOUT snapping, so two weights are ordered by what was actually on the bar. A weight entered in lb never outranks a heavier weight entered in kg, and two lb weights one pound apart stay distinguishable even though they display at the same kilogram increment.
vectors.reviewNote: Snapping before comparing would hide a real record: 225 lb and 226 lb both display as the same quarter-kilo. Comparison uses the raw converted value; display uses the snapped one.
